title: The Salvation Army
hookLine: William and Catherine Booth take soup, soap and salvation into the streets of London's East End

lines: A DRUM ON A STREET CORNER.
cards: A drum, then a cornet, then a few voices singing, off key and loud, on a street corner in the East End of London, outside a pub. People stop, some to listen, some to jeer. The singers wear uniforms.
Their leader is called the General. If it sounds like an army, that's the point: a church that decided to march into the poor streets instead of waiting for the poor to come to church.
It was started by a preacher named William Booth and his wife, Catherine, a preacher too. Today, a church with brass bands, ranks, and a pot of soup on the stove.

teach.b: The Booths' work began as the Christian Mission. The story goes that a report described it as a volunteer army, and William crossed out volunteer and wrote salvation.
However it happened, the name stuck, and so did the ranks and uniforms.

Catherine didn't stand behind her husband. She preached to crowds herself, and wrote in defense of women preaching, when women in the pulpit were hotly argued over. The Army gave women real leadership from its early days.
The Army became known by a short phrase: soup, soap, salvation. Feed people. Help them get clean, find a bed, find work.
And tell them about the love of God. Soup comes first: hungry people can't hear much.

teach.h: DEAL THY BREAD TO THE HUNGRY.
teach.b: The Booths could point to Isaiah, where God describes the fast he wants, in the King James Bible: "Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house?"
The Salvation Army is a church in its own right, with its own officers as ministers.
Salvationists don't hold baptism or communion services; they say the inner grace those rites point to is what counts, and they live it out in service.

Catholic and Orthodox churches, and Protestant churches such as Lutherans and Anglicans, hold those rites at the very center of their life. Both sides say so openly, and the Army works alongside other churches.
And salvation itself? In the Greek of the New Testament, it can mean rescue, safety and health, not only heaven. Soup, soap and salvation are three parts of one rescue.

how: Salvation Army corps hold Sunday worship with brass bands and run food banks, shelters and recovery programs, and its officers serve as both ministers and social workers.

games.q: you've been preaching on an East End street corner. the people listening haven't eaten today. what comes first?
o: tell them to come back when they're cleaned up.
games.why: the Army became known by soup, soap, salvation, and the soup comes first. Isaiah says it too: deal thy bread to the hungry.

practice: Picture the nearest place that feeds or shelters people, a food bank, a shelter, a church pantry, and then your own shelf: a can of soup, a bar of soap, a toothbrush still in its packet.
Choose one thing to set aside, and hold in mind the person who will open it. If you pray, pray for them.

wordCard.voice: William Booth. The preacher who, with his wife Catherine, founded the Salvation Army and crossed out volunteer for salvation in its name.

orig.note: Greek: salvation. it can also mean rescue, safety or health.
